title: Rationalize routing runtime and migrate fallback workers to evented state machine
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Background: The current smart-router runtime uses a mix of short-lived fallback goroutines, per-request locks, and ad-hoc regional heuristics that were added iteratively. This has caused increased p99 tail latency under bursty tenant load, noisy lock contention in the policy lookup path, and subtle races during regional failovers.

Goal: Replace the ad-hoc fallback goroutine pool with a single evented state machine that processes fallback decisions, reduce per-request locking by introducing read-optimized decision caches, and simplify region-affinity code paths. The work should lower p99 by ~15-25% for routing decisions, reduce CPU at high QPS, and make the codebase easier to reason about for future routing features.

Scope and high-level plan:
1) Fallback runtime: implement an evented state machine in router/fallback that sequences actions (probe, lease, escalate, failover) per-route instead of spinning per-request goroutines. Design will use a small fixed worker pool plus per-route state objects and an event queue.
2) Policy lookup: compile policy expressions to a compact evaluation form and add a read-mostly decision cache keyed by (tenant, route-hash, model-variant). Eviction is TTL + LRU for low memory overhead.
3) Region affinity: collapse duplicated region affinity heuristics into a single region-affinity service with explicit lease semantics and TTLs. Remove legacy per-request affinity recomputation.
4) Locking cleanup: replace several coarse-grained mutexes with sharded atomics and read-optimized structures to reduce contention on the hot path.
5) Dependency upgrades: bump protobuf (3.18 -> 3.26), grpc (1.46 -> 1.54) and Go to 1.20; validate compatibility and regenerate protos.
6) Telemetry and observability: add new metrics and traces (fallback_state_transitions, policy_cache_hit, region_lease_acquire_latency) and preserve old metric names as deprecated aliases for one release.
7) Tests and rollout: unit tests for state transitions, integration tests with synthetic stalls/failures, perf harness coverage for p50/p95/p99, staged canary rollout with traffic slicing and a 72-hour stabilization window.

Tradeoffs and constraints:
- The evented state machine simplifies reasoning but introduces a single coordination surface; we'll mitigate this with sharded queues and clear backpressure semantics.
- Policy compilation improves lookup speed but adds complexity in invalidation; we'll implement simple version tags and safe invalidation via a compare-and-swap update path.
- Dependency upgrades must be coordinated with infra teams (container images, build images).

Acceptance criteria:
- New fallback state machine passes unit tests and integration tests (no regressions on existing failover scenarios).
- End-to-end perf: routing-decision p99 improved by at least 12% on synthetic mixed-tenancy workload compared to baseline, and steady-state CPU usage reduced for top 10 tenants.
- Policy cache hit rate > 85% for stable workloads in synthetic benchmark.
- No customer-visible errors during canary; automated rollback trigger in console if error rate or latency exceeds baseline by configured thresholds.

Files/paths to change (non-exhaustive):
- router/fallback/state_machine.go (new)
- router/decision/compiler.go (policy compilation)
- router/decision/cache.go (read-optimized cache)
- router/region/affinity.go (consolidated service)
- internal/metrics/defs.yaml (add new metrics)

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement state machine, unit tests, policy compiler prototype (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (staging): integration tests, perf harness runs, dependency bumps in staging (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (canary): 5% traffic in region-us-west for 72 hours, run perf and error monitors (1 week)
- Phase 4 (gradual): increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% across regions with health gates and rollback automation (2–3 weeks)

Notes: See linked design doc for event model and state diagrams. We'll keep the legacy fallback code behind a feature flag for fast rollback.
acceptance_criteria: 1) fallback state machine unit/integration tests pass; 2) p99 routing-decision improves >=12% in perf harness; 3) policy cache hit rate >=85% under stable workload; 4) canary rollout shows no customer errors and meets latency SLOs; 5) metrics/traces emit and map correctly to dashboards
